title: Script reader notes (written by Claude, read by annotate.py and report.py)

lang.description: language of the notes (default: the script's)

structure.description: structure id the draft was read against (references/structures.json)

logline_read.description: the story in one line as the reader understood it; lets the writer see if it lands

text.description: the note: what you saw and a question for the writer; never a rewrite of their lines

quote.description: exact words from that scene to anchor the comment (optional)

row.description: documentary: the picture | sound row the note is about (anchors the comment there when no quote is given)

turns.description: beat id of the chosen structure → the scene where the script actually makes that turn (for the beat map); leave out beats the script doesn't have

tension.description: scene number (as text) → tension 0-5 as the reader felt it, every scene (for the tension curve)

previous.description: for a new draft: what happened to each note of the previous reading (ids from compare.py)

draft.description: which draft the previous notes were on, e.g. 1

text.description: the old note in a few words

scene.description: where it stands now (new scene number), if anywhere

intent_check.description: when the writer gave an intent sheet: does the script do what they are going for? One item per stated aim, open question or deliberate choice

intent.description: the writer's aim or question, in a few words

arcs.description: up to 3 main characters: how their inner state moves (for the arc chart). value -2 (lowest) .. +2 (highest); give points only where it changes

start.description: what they want or believe at the start, a few words

end.description: where they end, a few words

want.description: what they want in this scene, if it changed

cards.description: optional: scene number → the scene in one line (8-12 words) for the scene cards; else the first action line is used

scope.description: what this reading covers (default full). first-pages: how a festival reader meets the script; lenses: a focused pass (e.g. dialogue only)

lens_set.description: which viewpoints: film (references/lenses.json, default) or documentary (references/lenses_doc.json) for a treatment, A/V script or paper edit
